options.A: Shift entirely to premium pricing, because blue ocean is proven only when prices are raised continuously over time in practice
options.B: Shift entirely to low price, because blue ocean is proven only when prices are cut continuously over time in effect
options.C: Avoid trade-offs and keep adding features, because blue ocean requires being best on all dimensions for all buyers
options.D: Re-clarify trade-offs and align activities, because sustaining a coherent profile matters more than chasing every feature for buyers

questions.explanation: emphasizes coherence: leaders must clarify trade-offs and align actions to avoid drifting into the middle as markets evolve.

questions.stem: Apple Vision Pro attempts premium spatial computing. Which statement best captures what would qualify as “value innovation” in Session 12 terms?

options.A: A move that raises perceived value only, accepting higher costs and relying purely on premium pricing to compensate at scale
options.B: A move that raises perceived value while also lowering key costs, reconciling trade-offs rather than just adding features overall
options.C: A move that lowers costs only, reducing perceived value and relying purely on price cuts to create demand quickly in practice
options.D: A move that raises perceived value only, but called blue ocean because the category is new and competitors are absent

questions.explanation: Blue ocean strategy requires value innovation: simultaneously increasing value and reducing costs to reconcile trade-offs between differentiation and cost leadership.

questions.stem: Which action best matches the “eliminate” step in the eliminate–reduce–raise–create (ERRC) grid used in blue ocean analysis?

options.A: Keeping the same factors but changing the brand name, thereby creating new demand through awareness effects
options.B: Raising all existing factors above rivals, thereby proving superiority on every dimension at scale for buyers
options.C: Removing an industry factor that buyers no longer value, thereby cutting cost while sharpening focus at scale
options.D: Adding a new industry factor that buyers already get from rivals, thereby matching competition fully for buyers

questions.explanation: In the ERRC grid, “eliminate” targets taken-for-granted factors that add cost but little value. Eliminating them supports value innovation by lowering costs and clarifying the value curve.

questions.stem: Which condition most directly distinguishes a successful blue ocean move from a typical differentiation move?

options.A: Raising value while lowering key costs, rather than trading higher costs for higher value alone
options.B: Raising prices while raising value, because blue ocean is defined by premium pricing and exclusivity
options.C: Raising value while raising key costs, because blue ocean requires premium inputs and premium pricing
options.D: Lowering costs while lowering value, because blue ocean requires being cheapest even if quality suffers

questions.explanation: Blue ocean is defined by value innovation that reconciles value-cost trade-offs. Differentiation alone typically raises costs to raise value.

questions.stem: Which leadership implication is most consistent with Session 12 when a firm chooses a business-level strategy?

options.A: Leaders should choose low price first, because low price automatically determines the cost structure and value for rivals
options.B: Leaders should avoid trade-offs and keep options open, because strategic flexibility is always superior to focus
options.C: Leaders should choose premium pricing first, because pricing automatically determines the strategic position for buyers in effect
options.D: Leaders must make explicit trade-offs and align activities so the strategic profile stays coherent during execution

questions.explanation: ’s implication is disciplined strategic positioning: choose a coherent value–cost profile and align actions; without alignment, firms drift into the middle.

questions.stem: Which managerial practice best helps sustain a blue-ocean move once competitors begin to imitate parts of the offering?

options.A: Raise price sharply to signal premium status, because higher prices alone prevent imitation and restore uniqueness for rivals at scale
options.B: Avoid any further change, because stability prevents rivalry and therefore preserves new market space automatically for buyers over time
options.C: Chase every competitor feature quickly, even if it raises costs, because matching is the safest response to imitation for rivals
options.D: Protect and refresh the value curve by continuing ERRC-style redesign, while keeping activities aligned with the intended profile

questions.explanation: Imitation erodes uniqueness. Sustaining advantage requires ongoing alignment and renewal of the value curve - not random feature chasing that creates zigzags and “middle” outcomes.

questions.stem: Which sign most strongly indicates a firm is becoming “stuck in the middle” during execution?

options.A: The firm invests in a single differentiating feature, because single-feature strategies always fail in competitive markets in effect
options.B: The firm reduces prices, because price cuts always mean the firm lacks a coherent position and cannot recover
options.C: Activities pull in opposite directions, so costs rise while buyers do not perceive enough additional value to pay
options.D: The firm chooses a narrow niche, because focus automatically implies weak performance compared to broad strategies for buyers

questions.explanation: “Stuck in the middle” reflects incoherence: higher costs without commensurate buyer value, often caused by misaligned activities and unclear trade-offs.

questions.stem: Why is blue ocean strategy difficult to sustain, even when a firm succeeds initially?

options.A: Value innovation depends only on marketing, so rivals imitate ads but cannot imitate costs or operations in practice
options.B: Value innovation guarantees monopoly power, so rivals exit and buyer power collapses regardless of subsequent moves for rivals
options.C: Value innovation eliminates substitutes permanently, so rivals cannot imitate and entry barriers become irrelevant forever in effect in effect
options.D: Value innovation diffuses and rivals imitate, so the unique value-cost configuration can erode as competition catches up

questions.explanation: notes that exceptional profiles can diffuse; imitation and shifting trade-offs reappear, making sustained blue ocean hard.
